paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus finished it. The law was a shadow, and the sacrifices under it were an annual reminder of sins, because "it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins" (Hebrews 10:1, 3-4). But Jesus offered "one sacrifice for sins" for all time, and then He sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12). A priest who sits down is a priest whose work is DONE.

Now here's why it matters to you. By that single offering, He "has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified" (Hebrews 10:14). So you don't have to rebuild your standing with God every week with a fresh pile of effort. I used to think I had to earn my way back out of that junk drawer, and I had nothing to earn it with but dust and a 25 cent price sticker. The writer says we "have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all" (Hebrews 10:10).

And look at what God promises on top of it. "I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds," and "Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more" (Hebrews 10:16-17). Then the writer lands it: "where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed" (Hebrews 10:18). So bake with a clear conscience, friend. The payment is made, the forgiveness is real, and your heart is where God's Word gets written.
